title: Adaptive SSE sequence windows and graceful reconnect behavior
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive SSE framing and reconnect strategy that minimizes duplicate tokens, enables fast client resume across intermittent connections, and provides deterministic chunk provenance for debugging and replay. This ticket covers protocol design, server-side implementation, client handshake probes, and a staged rollout.

Background: Current SSE behavior shows duplicate or missing partial tokens when mobile clients reconnect frequently and when responses are interleaved with function/tool call frames. Existing tickets addressed resume tokens and chunk checksums but left gaps around variable-length sequence windows, efficient backfill for clients with limited state, and clear heuristics for when to drop vs. request a partial re-send.

Scope:
- Define a compact wire framing for chunks (metadata + payload) that is backward-compatible with current JSONL SSE stream consumers.
- Implement a sequence-window model (sliding window of recent chunk sequence numbers) to allow server to advertise resumable ranges.
- Add lightweight delta-checkpoint tokens that let clients request the minimal backfill (prefix vs. full message re-stream).
- Implement connection probe/handshake: client sends last-seen-window and an optional digest; server responds with resume advice: ACCEPT, BACKFILL(range), FULL_REPLAY.
- Make framing resilient to tool/function-call boundaries: atomic chunk markers when functioncall frames split across reconnections.
- Emit diagnostic provenance metadata per chunk (chunk_id, seq, parent_seq, source-model, quantization-hint) to aid postmortem and debugging while keeping the default payload compact.
- Metrics and SLOs: track resume success rate, duplicate-token rate, backfill bytes per reconnect, and reconnection latency.

Non-goals: building client SDK changes for all languages (we will ship server-side and a canonical Node/Python client patch), full rework of the transport layer, or introducing a binary protocol in this release.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Server emits framed SSE chunks with metadata header compatible with existing streaming parsers (new fields optional).
2) Handshake probe exchanges allow server to recommend a resume strategy and server fulfills BACKFILL requests within configured latency SLO.
3) Duplicate-token rate reduced by >80% for flaky mobile reconnections in internal tests.
4) Tool/function call frames maintain atomicity across reconnects with no loss of call boundaries in >99.9% of synthetic tests.
5) New provenance metadata available in logging and trace events; privacy review completed if any PII fields are proposed.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Stronger resume semantics require storing short-lived chunk windows per session; cost/scale trade-off for high-connection-count customers. We will cap window retention with an eviction policy and expose configurables per customer.
- Adding metadata increases payload size; default is compact header with opt-in detailed provenance.
- Backfill introduces load spikes when many clients reconnect simultaneously; design includes rate-limits and leaky-bucket smoothing on backfill serving.

Implementation notes:
- Wire framing: use a single-line JSON prefix header per chunk followed by a separator and then the token payload. Example chunk header (compact): {"cid":"c9f2","s":523,"p":522,"ck":"b64sha1","atomic":true}<<SEP>><payload>
- Sequence window: server maintains last N sequence numbers per session id and per connection lease. N default = 64, configurable at tenant level.
- Delta checkpoint token: opaque base64 token representing (session_id, last_seq, digest of last window). Clients present this in the initial SSE request as Resume-Token.
- Probe handshake: initial HTTP GET includes headers Resume-Token and Resume-Window. Server responds with HTTP 200 and first SSE comment line 'res:ADVICE;range=520-523' or 'res:FULL_REPLAY'.
- Atomic functioncall handling: server groups toolcall frames in a single atomic chunk when possible. If an atomic chunk is split, server includes 'atomic_fragment_index' and 'atomic_total_fragments' in headers so clients can reassemble deterministically.
- Backfill policy: server honors BACKFILL(range) up to a tenant-configured bytes cap (default 1MB). If request exceeds cap server returns BACKFILL_LIMITED and includes best-effort partial range.

Testing and validation:
- Load tests with 10k concurrent connections simulating mobile churn (500ms disconnects) to measure duplicate-token and backfill overhead.
- Fault-injection tests: partial chunk loss, out-of-order delivery, and simultaneous reconnection storms.
- End-to-end integration tests with node/python canonical clients validating handshake and atomic functioncall reassembly.
- Security review for provenance metadata to ensure no PII or sensitive tokens leak.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gating at tenant-level (experimental) and internal dogfood tenants.
2) Deploy server implementation in staging; run synthetic churn tests, iterate on heuristics.
3) Enable for 5 internal tenants for 2 weeks; monitor metrics.
4) Gradually roll to more tenants with opt-in console toggle; enable default after 6 weeks and positive metrics.

Observability:
- New metrics: streaming.resume.requests, streaming.resume.success, streaming.backfill.bytes, streaming.duplicate_tokens, streaming.atomic_reassembly_failures.
- Traces: each chunk emitted logs chunk_id, seq, lease-id, and resume-token used.
- Dashboards: 1) Resume success heatmap by tenant, 2) Backfill bandwidth by region, 3) Duplicate-token trend.

Migration and compatibility:
- Backwards compatible: clients that do not send Resume-Token will receive no-backfill advice and continue to stream from start.
- For older clients, the server will still emit minimal headers and include a comment line summarizing non-actionable resume state to avoid parser breakage.

Links to artifacts: see links field for design doc, canary plan, and initial prototype PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Framed chunks use an optional JSON header prefix followed by payload separator for backward compatibility
Server handshake returns resume advice and satisfies BACKFILL requests within 200ms p50 for staging workloads
Duplicate tokens reduced by >80% under synthetic mobile reconnect load
Atomic functioncall boundaries preserved across reconnects in >99.9% of tests
Provenance metadata available in logs without exposing PII
technical_notes: Chunk header fields: cid (8 hex), s (seq int), p (parent seq), ck (base64 checksum), atomic (bool), af_i (fragment idx), af_t (total)
Use Redis TTL'd stream windows keyed by session lease for short-term window retention; fallback to local in-memory for single-server lease owner
Backfill implementation streams historical chunks as SSE events with controlled rate limiting and request-level budget enforcement
Canonical clients to implement parser that tolerates single-line JSON header or absence of header and treats lines after <<SEP>> as payload
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start internal tenants only
Monitor resume.success and duplicate_tokens for 2 weeks in dogfood tenants
Enable tenant opt-in in console with per-tenant window size configuration
Default-on after 6 weeks if key metrics stable
qa_tests: Reconnect with last_seq present and verify server issues BACKFILL(range) and client reassembles payload
Simulate atomic functioncall split across reconnect and assert reassembly correctness
Stress test: 10k mobile-churn connections and measure duplicate-token rate reduction
Edge: client with invalid Resume-Token receives FULL_REPLAY and stream remains parsable
